Authentic
Dec 2017
We walked beyond Notre Dame Cathedral as far as Nguyen Van Chien St looking for a local restaurant. Thanh Nien had a range of set menus from which to choose, and a buffet was also on offer for 28 000VD. We settled on that and took a table in the air conditioned section in preference to eating outdoors.
Several live cooking stations were set up - barbecue, noodle, etc - and soup, salads, seafood, curry and meat dishes were constantly replenished. Desserts of fresh fruit, sago pudding and cakes were offered, as were drinks (cordial?) and ice cream. We were uncertain what some of the dishes were, but it all seemed fresh and was tasty.
This was very much a local restaurant and many family groups were present on a Saturday evening. It is the sort of place you stumble across, or go with a local. We enjoyed the experience and considered it value for money. We struggled with language but the staff members were friendly and helpful. A genuine local experience not pitched at the tourist.

They need a "do-over" but we won't
May 2016 • Couples
The setting is nice and the menu large enough to include many traditional delights, but somewhere in the kitchen there isn't the skill to really make the food as good as Vietnamese cuisine can be. More subtlety, more nuance, more freshness in the approach could make this workable again, but the status quo isn't working.

It's a marvelous come back!
Nov 2014
I've been away from the country for some times since my last visit to Thanh Nien Restaurant. And it was a HUGE SURPRISE when my brother took me there for dinner: the restaurant beautifully renovated and look busy as it used to be 25 years ago!
Comes to the food, we ordered Vietnamese traditional dishes Spring Rolls (Cha Gio), Lotus Salad with Tiger Prawns, Fried Rice with Chicken and Bamboo Shoot in Clay Pot, and Sauteed Crab in Tamarind Sauce. These dishes are served in adequate portion and full of flavours! I really love the tamarind crab while my brother and the wives adore the spring rolls. It's fair enough to say Thanh Nien Restaurant is one of the few in HCMC can satisfy both local's and tourists' tastes!
The service was not a top notch one but friendly and warmy enough to feel this is a family style restaurant.
There was one thing I noticed: the Piano Bar is not there, and so the buffet! The manager told us the daily buffet will be re-kicked off soon, which is good news for me (((-:
On the downside, the service speed was just average, sometimes you have to wait a few minutes for the next dish while you're excited with the previous one.
Oh, before this review becomes too long, I just want to recommend you guys to try the desert menu, especially local sweets.
I give this place a 8,5 out of 10.

Good food at Thanh Nien!
Oct 2012 • Friends
The restaurant's full name is NHA HANG THANH NIEN and it is right across the Diamond Plaza Mall. 

We went there for lunch hoping for a buffet but found that there is buffet for dinner only. But no matter, we asked for an indoor seating (airconditioned) and we were led to one. What we liked in Thanh Nien is that the Menu has pictures and English description of each dish and their respective prices. We liked everything that we ordered. Service is fast enough and our lunch waiter had an acceptable ability speaking English. He had no problem recommending some items for us or understanding us when we were following up our orders. 

We also had dinner buffet and a la carte dinner in Thanh Nien. The dinner buffet included free drinks as well. You can choose from sodas and ginseng tea. Dishes include appetizers (mostly shell food during our buffet), main courses, different noodles where you can experiment on your own, fruits, and various rice cake desserts. Dishes include seafood, beef, chicken, and pork menus. There were very little vegetable choices during our buffet.

Our a la carte lunch cost us VND 678,000.00 with 4 drinks, Cantonese Fried Rice (good for 3), steamed rice (good for 2), Shrimp & Cauliflower, Cha Gio (Spring Rolls), Crispy Fried Squid and Pork in Clay Pot. Our a la carte dinner cost us VND 750,000 with 2 drinks, Cantonese Fried Rice, Steamed Rice, Cha Gio, Kangkong with Garlic, Crispy Fried Squid, Marinated Pork and Tofu with Garlic. Cost of Dinner Buffet is VND 180,000.00 per person.

It is true that a lot of locals eat in this resto, whether a la carte or in the buffet. Hence, if locals frequent it, it must be good!

All in all, good food, good surroundings and good price! We recommend this and we'd come back if ever we're back in HCM!

Excellent authentic Vietnamese Buffet for reasonable prices!
Jun 2012 • Couples
We dined at this buffet restaurant last night, on our first day of return visit to Ho Chi Minh City. To say the least, we couldn't wait! The exact name of the restaurant is "Nha Hang Thanh Nien" (translation, "Youth Restaurant", and it is one of our favorites, on each of our many visits to HCM City.

First, the atmosphere is warm and pleasant. It makes us feel like we are dining in a place in the country side, although it is right in the heart of the city, by the Grand Cathedral ("Nha Tho Duc Ba"). Outside the restaurant, it is a part of town in full energy, even late into the evening, because of its proximity to where the young people hang out every night. But inside, you have the feeling on dining in a warm atmosphere in a smaller town in the suburn. The restaurant is large, for Vietnamese standard. The bus boys (mostly male) are nice and courteous. But of course, the main reason for being here is because of the restaurant's food!

What is striking about this one is its variety and large selection of fresh and typical Vietnamese food. It is not catered for tourists (foreigners), although there are always packed buses unloading several dozens of tourists at a time, most of them are Vietnamese tourists though. You have at the counters most of traditional Vietnamese dishes, like "bun bo hue", "bun rieu", Vietnamese eggrolls and springrolls, "banh beo", "banh bot chien", and plenty of sea food ("oc", in particular), etc. The dessert is excellent, and there is a large variety and selection to choose from. The drinks are also worth mentioning, especially "tra sam" (some sort of Vietnamese herbal tea drink).

All in all, it's worth the money and it offers a typical taste of Vietnamese food, particularly when you are on a short visit to town.

Delicious Food, Fabulous service - worth more than one visit.
Apr 2011
We arrived in Saigon in the evening and the hotel suggested Thanh Nien for a buffet meal (under $8Aust each included soft drink). A cheap cab ride from District One (40,000VND = $2 AUD) and we were there! Fabulous service, DELICIOUS food and with the buffet it meant we could try all sorts of different Vietnamese food. We returned for another meal at then end of our travels, this time from the menu, none of us were dissapointed. Le looked after us so well. He even brought out the 2nd lot of beers in an ice bucket to keep them extra chilled. Both times we chose to sit out in the garden area under the large bamboo it was so peaceful and relaxing it was hard to believe we weren't sitting in a resort. Total cost for meals for 5 people with 2 drinks each, came to under 700,000 VND, (approx $35). Go and enjoy - We did, even the Vegetarian was thrilled with her combination noodles (with no meat or seafood). We were all so sorry we didn't get to return one last time to eat up, thank them all and say goodbye.

Delcious vietnamese food for a very good price
This vietnamese food restaurant was one of the best choices I had during my days in Ho Chi Minh. Big, with some tables in the garden, and tables in air conditioned rooms. I found it in a Japanese guide book and decided to give it a try. Opens at 06:00PM, closes at 10:00PM. Very popular with local and with Asian tourists. It has a good buffet (sea food, hot pots, noodles, rices, meats, grilled dishes) that will cost around 140,000 dongs around US$9 per person. Kids pay half. They also have an extensive menu. The drink menu goes as in other restaurants, but I'm not quite sure about the wine list. As the restaurant attracts a lot of vietnamese families, its wise to get there earlier for dinner. Or ask your hotel to make a reservation for you. If your flight departures late at night (as it was my case), this could be a very good option to have your last vietnamese food bite. Just be sure to be at 6:00PM to be the first in the buffet.
